children: India's real estate sector has remained resilient in the first two months of 2QFY27F, with most major launches lined up for September, Nomura said in its latest India real estate round-up.
The brokerage said its discussions with mass-market players including Prestige Estates, Godrej Properties andLodha had not indicated any slowdown in sustenance sales from existing inventory.
"Sustenance sales remain largely in-line with respective companies' business plans," Nomura said.

Several high-profile launches are scheduled for September, following Oberoi Realty's 360 North launch in July. These include Godrej Properties' Verano in NCR, with a ticket size of around Rs 70 million per unit; Godrej Properties' Bandra Bay in Mumbai Metropolitan Region at Rs 350-400 million per unit; DLF's Aureva in NCR at Rs 120 million per unit; and Brigade's Neopolis Phase 2 in Hyderabad at Rs 35-40 million per unit.

Nomura said a prolonged Middle East conflict and its consequent impact on macroeconomic conditions and customer sentiment remained a key risk. "Prestige Estates (PEPL IN, Buy) remains our top sector pick," it said.
Prestige Estates

Nomura expects Prestige Estates to launch projects with an approximate gross development value (GDV) of Rs 50 billion in 2QFY27F. These include Garden Breeze at The Prestige City in Bangalore with a GDV of Rs 10.5 billion, Avon in Bangalore at Rs 5.5 billion, Springwood in Bangalore at Rs 2.9 billion, Battersea in Bangalore at Rs 19 billion and Palm Court in Chennai at Rs 12 billion.
RERA approval is pending for Garden Breeze, Avon, Springwood and Battersea, while Palm Court has received approval and has been launched.
Lodha
Lodha's Beaumont Estate in Bangalore, with a GDV of Rs 20 billion, has received RERA approval and has been launched. Nomura's channel checks indicate strong demand for the project.
"As per management, sustenance sales across projects remain in line with business plans," the brokerage said.
Godrej Properties
Godrej Properties' Verano project on 63A Golf Course Extension Road has a GDV of Rs 45 billion, with RERA approval received and the launch expected in September.

Bandra Bay in Bandra, with a GDV of around Rs 60-70 billion, is awaiting RERA approval and could be launched either by the end of September or in October. Regent Park in Bangalore, with a GDV of Rs 10-12 billion for the first phase, has received RERA approval and has already been launched.
Nomura has a 'Neutral' rating on Godrej Properties.
Oberoi Realty

Oberoi Realty's 360 North, with a GDV of Rs 80 billion, was launched and sold out at the beginning of the quarter. No other launches are planned during the quarter, while management said sustenance sales across projects remain in line with business plans.
Nomura has a 'Buy' rating on Oberoi Realty.
DLF

DLF's Senior Living, Arbour Phase 2, with a GDV of Rs 20-25 billion, has received RERA approval and is expected to launch in mid-September. Nomura's channel checks indicate strong demand for the project.
The brokerage has a 'Buy' rating on DLF.
ABREL
For Aditya Birla Real Estate, Nomura expects the third tower of Birla Niyara in Worli, Mumbai, to be launched towards the end of 2QFY27F or in 3QFY27F.
Nomura has a 'Buy' rating on ABREL.
Brigade

Brigade's Neopolis Phase 2 in Hyderabad has received RERA approval. Nomura's channel checks indicate resilient demand despite the relatively large ticket size of Rs 35-40 million per unit for the region.
Brigade is not rated by Nomura.

title: September launches to drive India real estate; Nomura names Prestige Estates top pick
